messages:
Alice: Quick RFC follow-up — I sketched a small refactor for the ingest mesh so the contract boundary lives at the mesh ingress rather than in the enrichment workers. Goal: reduce downstream amplification and make billing attribution decisions deterministic earlier in the pipeline. Thinking incremental rollout across regions.

Ben: Sounds promising. major question: how do we keep cost attribution stable during the transition? if ingress decides billing keys, will queries that expect ‘old’ keys break?

Alice: Good point. Plan is to emit both keys during a grace window: ingress will set billing_key_v2 and keep billing_key_v1. We then run a backfill/compare job for 2 weeks and switch consumers to v2.

Chandra: Must ensure schema gating so older consumers don't explode on unexpected fields. Suggest a header flag `X-Ingest-Contract-Version` and a server-side toggle to strip unknown attrs for legacy routes. Also watch cardinality on any new derived attrs.

Marta: For rollout: feature-flag + canary in us-west-2 with 10% traffic, collect cost deltas and cardinality metrics. We should set a cleanup TTL for billing_key_v1 after 30d.

Ben: Query shape note: moving key selection earlier will change indexing since billing_key becomes part of shard key. We need to model how many unique keys we expect. if it grows >10x, cost will blow up. do we have an estimator?

Alice: We have sample histograms from last month; attaching quick example below (pseudo):

```
// envelope example emitted at ingress
{
  "envelope_id": "env_123",
  "service": "redwood-api",
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "billing_key_v1": "acct:acme",
  "billing_key_v2": "tenant:acme:env:prod",
  "attrs": {"model":"m-13b","seq_len":512}
}
```

Chandra: That v2 looks higher cardinality (tenant + env). we need a normalization step or fingerprinting for low-volume tenants so they don't create index churn. maybe map rare tenants into `tenant:fallback` for billing-aggregation until they hit a threshold.

Marta: Ops checklist:
- Flag: roll_ingress_contract_v2 (FF key)
- Canary: us-west-2 10%
- Metrics: billing_key_cardinality, unique_billing_keys_1h, query_latency_95
- Backfill: compare_v1_v2 job (dry-run)
- TTL: drop_v1_after_30d

devops-bot: CI pipeline triggered: `ingest-contract-refactor` build #482 -> canary image pushed to us-west-2 staging. See: https://ci.internal/redwood/482 :rocket:

Ben: Also add a regression eval for cost-per-request; if cost increases >5% on canary we halt and rollback.

Alice: Agreed. Also need an explicit compatibility test suite for consumers breaking on extra fields (strip vs strict modes). Chandra can you own that?

Chandra: I can. I'll add a compatibility matrix doc and a test harness that replays real envelopes against strict/lenient parsers. ETA end of next week.

David: I can own rollout ops and the backfill job. Will coordinate with infra for index pre-splits if cardinality spikes.

Marta: One more: monitoring alert if unique_billing_keys_1h climbs > 25% above baseline during canary. add to runbook.

Alice: Owners & next steps: Alice (design + roadmap), Chandra (compat tests), David (backfill + ops), Marta (rollout + runbook), Ben (cost gating). Meeting Friday 10am PT to sign off. Thanks everyone :+1:
